thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Streaming p99 latency breach detected on /v1/stream (region: us-central1). p95 1.7s, p99 5.9s over 7m. Error rate +3.1%. Possible streaming stalls.

alex.ng: paging oncall @marcel @jamal. getting customer reports of mid-stream freezes. any immediate visibility?

pria.singh: I'm seeing many traces with repeated backpressure in send loop, span=stream.write_chunk. It looks like a small subset of GPU nodes are saturating their PCIe link then dropping writes. Affected nodes: gpu-21 and gpu-26 (pool gpu-inference-pool-2).

jamal: pulling telemetry now. GPU utilization for pool-2 is normal overall but gpu-21 shows sustained 99% utilization and GI stats show many ECC corrected events. nvml: ecc_corrected=120 in 15m for gpu-21. dmesg has repeated "GPU ECC error corrected" entries.

infra-sre: confirmed ECC spikes and thermal climbs to ~90C on gpu-21. Also seeing `pcieport 0000:3b:00.0: AER: Corrected error received` log lines. Looks like hardware-level instability.

sophie: CS opened three tickets for affected customers (CS-5010, CS-5011, CS-5012). Customers describe partial transcripts then long silence then reconnect. Flagging enterprise customers: OmniData and Streamly.

marcel: oncall here. First step: remove suspected nodes from LB and drain. Then apply emergency model fallback to q4 quantized variant for remaining capacity. Also enable fast routing failover for the route.

jamal: issuing cordon+drain for gpu-21/gpu-26: `kubectl cordon gpu-21 && kubectl drain gpu-21 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=30` (and same for gpu-26).

(priya.singh posts a trace snippet)
```
req-id: req-cc9f3a
span: stream.write_chunk
observed: repeated 500ms block then resume
node: gpu-21
nvml: ecc_incr: 18 -> 120 over 15m
```

alex.ng: routing change applied: shifting weights away from pool-2: `routing set-weight /v1/stream pool-2=0 pool-1=60 pool-3=40`. Will monitor; reverting if adverse.

incident-bot: Incident created INC-2026-03-14-1945678901 severity SEV2. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-hardware-degradation>. Paging @marcel @infra-sre.

marcel: connecting to BMC for gpu-21. I'll try soft powercycle after drain completes then monitor ECC counters. If counts continue increasing, mark for RMA.

infra-sre: drain progress: gpu-21 drained (6/6 pods rescheduled), gpu-26 draining (4/6). After routing and drain, p95 back to ~180ms, p99 ~470ms; error rate trending down.

jamal: model-fallback applied: `reconfig route /v1/stream --model chat-main-q4` to reduce memory pressure and help remaining nodes. No errors on replaced pods so far.

sophie: CS notifications sent at 1945679200 to affected customers with short summary + mitigation. OmniData asked whether dedicated nodes are impacted; they were using cross-pool fallback so saw minimal effect.

marcel: performing BMC soft reboot on gpu-21: `ipmitool -I lanplus -H bmc.gpu-21 -U admin -P **** chassis power cycle`. ETA 2m.

infra-sre: post-reboot nvml shows ECC counters reset but then increasing again: 27 in 4m. Thermal at idle 82C. This is suspicious for hardware defect rather than transient heat.

priya.singh: replayed failing traces against pool-1 as a regression check; no stalls observed under fallback model. That suggests problem is localized to nodes rather than model/runtime.

alex.ng: action item: keep node offline and open hardware replacement ticket. Also collect full PCIe AER logs, nvml dumps, and kernel oops if any.

jamal: quarantine command: `infra quarantine-node gpu-21 --owner marcel --tag ecc-2026-03-14`. Also created HW ticket HW-9873 for RMA.

marcel: handoff to afternoon oncall @jamal at 1945679500. Summary for handoff: SEV2 due to GPU hardware ECC/thermal causing p99 streaming stalls. Mitigation: drained offending nodes, routed traffic away, applied model fallback; nodes quarantined and RMA opened. Customer impact: ~3-5% of streaming sessions in us-central1, three CS tickets, SLO breach window ~9m.

jamal: ack taking handoff. I'll monitor for recurrence and follow up with HW ops on RMA ETA.

customer-success-bot: CS updated and status page posted. Customers asked for RCA — will provide after postmortem.

pria.singh: I'll draft the postmortem and attach traces + timeline. Adding request ids: req-cc9f3a, req-bb8b2c, req-dd7e11.

infra-sre: also raising follow-up item to tighten paging thresholds: ECC corrected X events within Y minutes -> page oncall earlier. Owner: infra-sre.

incident-bot: Incident status: Mitigated -> Monitoring. Will reopen automatically if metrics regress.

marcel: final note: good ops by team. keep an eye on cluster-wide ECC counts; if we see a cluster-level trend, we may need a broader kernel/driver review. :thumbsup:

jamal: monitoring continues. Closing the loop here unless anything else comes up.
